prompt.content:
You are a power system operator scheduling generation across 6 consecutive time periods.

Online units (all committed for the whole horizon; note that cheaper units ramp slowly and fast units are expensive):
  G1: cost $50.1/MWh, output range [49.0, 142.5] MW, max output change between consecutive periods 23.2 MW
  G2: cost $18.89/MWh, output range [99.9, 259.4] MW, max output change between consecutive periods 38.8 MW
  G3: cost $46.91/MWh, output range [89.6, 259.1] MW, max output change between consecutive periods 46.7 MW
  G4: cost $48.08/MWh, output range [96.4, 267.0] MW, max output change between consecutive periods 75.9 MW
  G5: cost $113.13/MWh, output range [22.2, 168.2] MW, max output change between consecutive periods 144.2 MW

System load by period:
  Period 1: 399.5 MW
  Period 2: 407.0 MW
  Period 3: 646.7 MW
  Period 4: 905.2 MW
  Period 5: 909.1 MW
  Period 6: 745.0 MW

Find the schedule that minimizes total cost ($) such that, in every period,
total generation equals that period's load and every unit is within its output
range — AND no unit's output changes by more than its ramp limit between one
period and the next. The first period has no prior-period constraint.

Report each MW value to at least one decimal place. Constraints are verified
with a +/-0.5 MW tolerance, but imbalance or limit violations inside that
tolerance are penalized in the cost scoring, so target exact feasibility.

Respond with your final answer as JSON on the last line, exactly in this format
(one inner list per period, 5 values per list, unit order as given):
{"dispatch_mw": [[<G1 MW>, <G2 MW>, <G3 MW>, <G4 MW>, <G5 MW>], ... one list per period ...]}
